questions.question: You’re at a café and your friend’s coffee is cold. What would be the most appropriate way to ask for a replacement?
options: I’m sorry, could you bring me another coffee? It’s too cold.
Your coffee is too cold, just get another one.
I think your coffee is ruined, let’s get a new one.
I’m not sure if I should ask for a replacement—maybe I’ll just wait.
questions.answer: I’m sorry, could you bring me another coffee? It’s too cold.

questions.question: Your colleague suggests taking a break to relax. How would you respond if you agree but want to add a suggestion for the next activity?
options: Yes, let’s take a break. Then maybe we should play a quick game of chess?
Okay, but we should definitely go outside for some fresh air instead.
I think we should just sit here and chat for a while.
A break sounds good, but I’d prefer to watch a film instead.
questions.answer: Yes, let’s take a break. Then maybe we should play a quick game of chess?

questions.question: You’re explaining to a friend why you can’t meet for coffee tomorrow. What would be the most polite way to request a different time?
options: I’m sorry, but I can’t meet tomorrow—I’ve got a prior commitment.
Tomorrow is impossible—I’ll meet you next week instead.
You’re too busy tomorrow? That’s fine, I’ll just cancel.
I’m sorry, but I can’t make it tomorrow—I’ll see you later.
questions.answer: I’m sorry, but I can’t meet tomorrow—I’ve got a prior commitment. Can we try next Friday?

questions.question: At a formal dinner, your neighbour says, ‘This dish is not to my taste.’ How would you respond if you want to politely agree but also suggest an alternative?
options: I see, I agree. Maybe we should try the dessert instead?
That’s true, it’s not very good. I’d prefer the main course.
This dish is fine, but I’ll have the wine with it.
I don’t like this dish, but I’ll eat it anyway.
questions.answer: I see, I agree. Maybe we should try the dessert instead?

questions.question: Your boss asks you to help with a project, but you’re already overloaded with tasks. What would be the most appropriate way to politely decline and offer an alternative?
options: I’m really sorry, but I can’t take on more work right now—I’ve got enough on my plate.
No, I don’t think I can help with that—I’m busy with something else.
I’ll help if you want, but I’ll have to leave early.
I can’t do that, but I’ll see if someone else can take it over.
questions.answer: I’m really sorry, but I can’t take on more work right now—I’ve got enough on my plate. Would you be open to me delegating this to [Colleague’s Name]?
